accepted.s: Jim Corbett National Park was originally established in 1936 under which name?
accepted.x: Jim Corbett National Park was established in 1936 as Hailey National Park and is recognised as India’s first national park.
accepted.tq: Use the direct year–name association for the first national park.
accepted.sec: National Parks, Tiger Reserves and sanctuaries → state; newest tiger reserves

accepted.s: Keoladeo National Park, also known as Bharatpur, is located in which State?
accepted.x: Keoladeo National Park is situated at Bharatpur in Rajasthan and is also a Ramsar site.
accepted.tq: Test the protected-area–State association directly.
accepted.sec: National Parks, Tiger Reserves and sanctuaries → state; newest tiger reserves

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Kanha Tiger Reserve — Madhya Pradesh
2. Askot Wildlife Sanctuary — Uttarakhand
3. Palamau Tiger Reserve — Jharkhand
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Kanha is in Madhya Pradesh, Askot is in Uttarakhand, and Palamau is in Jharkhand.
accepted.tq: Check each protected-area–State pair independently before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: National Parks, Tiger Reserves and sanctuaries → state; newest tiger reserves

accepted.s: Madhav Tiger Reserve, recognised as India’s 58th tiger reserve, is located in which State?
accepted.x: Madhav Tiger Reserve is situated in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh, and is the 58th tiger reserve.
accepted.tq: Link the ordinal number with the corresponding reserve and State.
accepted.sec: National Parks, Tiger Reserves and sanctuaries → state; newest tiger reserves

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the 56th tiger reserve of India?
accepted.x: Guru Ghasidas-Tamor Pingla Tiger Reserve in Chhattisgarh is the 56th tiger reserve.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely numbered newly designated reserves.
accepted.sec: National Parks, Tiger Reserves and sanctuaries → state; newest tiger reserves

accepted.s: Ratapani Tiger Reserve is associated with which State and ordinal position among India’s tiger reserves?
accepted.x: Ratapani Tiger Reserve is in Madhya Pradesh and is the 57th tiger reserve.
accepted.tq: Separate the adjacent 56th, 57th and 58th designations carefully.
accepted.sec: National Parks, Tiger Reserves and sanctuaries → state; newest tiger reserves

accepted.s: Project Tiger was launched with how many tiger reserves and what area in 1973?
accepted.x: Project Tiger began in 1973 with 9 tiger reserves covering 18,278 sq km.
accepted.tq: Match the initial programme figures rather than the current figures.
accepted.sec: National Parks, Tiger Reserves and sanctuaries → state; newest tiger reserves

accepted.s: Which State has the highest number of tiger reserves in India?
accepted.x: Madhya Pradesh has 9 tiger reserves, the highest number among Indian States.
accepted.tq: Use the superlative State–number association.
accepted.sec: National Parks, Tiger Reserves and sanctuaries → state; newest tiger reserves

accepted.s: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) is correctly described as which of the following?
o: A constitutional body headed by the Chief Justice of India
A statutory body under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, headed by the Environment Minister
A non-statutory body headed by the Prime Minister
A statutory body under the Forest Conservation Act, 1980, headed by the Home Minister
accepted.x: The NTCA is a statutory body under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, and is headed by the Environment Minister.
accepted.tq: Ask who created the body and who heads it to avoid authority-based traps.
accepted.sec: National Parks, Tiger Reserves and sanctuaries → state; newest tiger reserves

accepted.s: India has how many Biosphere Reserves and how many of them are included in UNESCO’s World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
accepted.x: India has 18 Biosphere Reserves, of which 13 are included in UNESCO’s World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total number from the UNESCO-listed subset.
accepted.sec: Biosphere Reserves → state, area ranking, UNESCO MAB listed vs not listed

accepted.s: Which was the first Biosphere Reserve established in India?
accepted.x: Nilgiri was India’s first Biosphere Reserve, designated in 1986.
accepted.tq: Use the first-in-sequence fact with its establishment year.
accepted.sec: Biosphere Reserves → state, area ranking, UNESCO MAB listed vs not listed

accepted.s: The largest Biosphere Reserve in India by area is:
accepted.x: The Great Rann of Kutch in Gujarat is the largest Indian Biosphere Reserve by area.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct superlative from the area comparison.
accepted.sec: Biosphere Reserves → state, area ranking, UNESCO MAB listed vs not listed

accepted.s: Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve is located in Andhra Pradesh and covers approximately:
accepted.x: Seshachalam is Andhra Pradesh’s only Biosphere Reserve. It covers 4,755.997 sq km and was notified in 2010.
accepted.tq: Test the exact area figure and the State-specific identification together.
accepted.sec: Biosphere Reserves → state, area ranking, UNESCO MAB listed vs not listed

accepted.s: Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, associated with the Kani tribe, extends over which States?
accepted.x: Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve extends across Tamil Nadu and Kerala and is associated with the Kani tribe.
accepted.tq: Use the two-State extent as the distinguishing feature.
accepted.sec: Biosphere Reserves → state, area ranking, UNESCO MAB listed vs not listed

accepted.s: Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve joined UNESCO’s World Network of Biosphere Reserves in:
accepted.x: Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve was included in UNESCO’s network in 2016.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the designation years of different reserves.
accepted.sec: Biosphere Reserves → state, area ranking, UNESCO MAB listed vs not listed

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Biosphere Reserves:
1. They are designated under UNESCO’s Man and the Biosphere Programme.
2. Their designation automatically changes land ownership.
3. Funding is shared in the ratio 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and 60:40 for other States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Biosphere Reserve designation does not change land ownership, so statement 2 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the false statement by checking the legal effect of designation.
accepted.sec: Biosphere Reserves → state, area ranking, UNESCO MAB listed vs not listed

accepted.s: The Ramsar Convention primarily deals with:
o: Conservation and wise use of wetlands
Control of international trade in minerals
accepted.x: The Ramsar Convention provides a framework for the conservation and wise use of wetlands.
accepted.tq: Test the exact purpose of the international convention.
accepted.sec: Ramsar sites and wetlands → state, latest additions, Convention purpose

accepted.s: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar in which country?
accepted.x: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran. India became a party to it in 1982.
accepted.tq: Separate the venue country from similarly named regional countries.
accepted.sec: Ramsar sites and wetlands → state, latest additions, Convention purpose

accepted.s: India joined the Ramsar Convention in:
accepted.x: India joined the Ramsar Convention in 1982.
accepted.tq: Use the country’s accession year rather than the convention’s adoption year.
accepted.sec: Ramsar sites and wetlands → state, latest additions, Convention purpose

accepted.s: As of August 2026, which Ramsar site became India’s 101st Ramsar site and Arunachal Pradesh’s first?
accepted.x: Glaw Lake in Arunachal Pradesh became India’s 101st Ramsar site on 3 August 2026 and was the State’s first Ramsar site.
accepted.tq: Combine the ordinal number, date and State to resolve a current-affairs fact.
accepted.sec: Ramsar sites and wetlands → state, latest additions, Convention purpose

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Ramsar site)
A. JP Narayan Bird Sanctuary / Surha Tal
B. Shekha Jheel
C. Khichan and Menar
D. Kopra Reservoir
List-II (State)

accepted.sec: Ramsar sites and wetlands → state, latest additions, Convention purpose

accepted.s: Which of the following is the Ramsar site of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Kolleru is Andhra Pradesh’s Ramsar site. Gogabeel is in Bihar, Glaw Lake is in Arunachal Pradesh, and Menar is in Rajasthan.
accepted.tq: Use State-specific identification among recently listed wetlands.
accepted.sec: Ramsar sites and wetlands → state, latest additions, Convention purpose

accepted.s: India ranks first in Asia and third in the world in terms of the number of Ramsar sites, as stated for August 2026. Which number of sites corresponds to this position?
accepted.x: India had 101 Ramsar sites as of August 2026 and was stated to rank first in Asia and third in the world.
accepted.tq: Use the dated count rather than an earlier or approximate figure.
accepted.sec: Ramsar sites and wetlands → state, latest additions, Convention purpose

accepted.s: Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary, noted as the smallest wildlife sanctuary in Andhra Pradesh, is located in:
accepted.x: Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary is in Andhra Pradesh and is noted as the State’s smallest wildlife sanctuary.
accepted.tq: Use the State-specific qualifying description to identify the sanctuary.
accepted.sec: Bird sanctuaries and species projects → state (first bird sanctuary, Project Tiger, Project Cheetah, GIB case)

accepted.s: Project Cheetah was launched in India on 17 September 2022 and involved which distinctive conservation activity?
o: The world’s first intercontinental translocation of a large carnivore
The first captive breeding of the Great Indian Bustard
The first reintroduction of tigers into India
The first translocation of elephants from Africa to India
accepted.x: Project Cheetah was the world’s first intercontinental large-carnivore translocation and began in India on 17 September 2022.
accepted.tq: Link the project date to its distinctive objective rather than a generic wildlife activity.
accepted.sec: Bird sanctuaries and species projects → state (first bird sanctuary, Project Tiger, Project Cheetah, GIB case)

accepted.s: The first batch of eight cheetahs under Project Cheetah was brought to Kuno National Park from:
accepted.x: Eight cheetahs were brought from Namibia to Kuno National Park in 2022. Twelve more came from South Africa in February 2023.
accepted.tq: Separate the source country and year of the first batch from the later batch.
accepted.sec: Bird sanctuaries and species projects → state (first bird sanctuary, Project Tiger, Project Cheetah, GIB case)

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the additional sites associated with the expansion of Project Cheetah after Kuno National Park?
o: Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary as the third home and Kanha Tiger Reserve as the second
Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary as the second home and Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve as the third
Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve as the second home and Palamau Tiger Reserve as the third
Kanha Tiger Reserve as the second home and Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary as the third
accepted.x: Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary is the second home for cheetahs and Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve is the third.
accepted.tq: Preserve the sequence of locations rather than merely recognising the names.
accepted.sec: Bird sanctuaries and species projects → state (first bird sanctuary, Project Tiger, Project Cheetah, GIB case)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Great Indian Bustard:
1. Its principal States mentioned are Rajasthan and Gujarat.
2. Its population is fewer than 150 birds.
3. The Supreme Court’s 2024 position retained underground power lines in priority habitats and allowed bird diverters elsewhere.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Great Indian Bustard is associated with Rajasthan and Gujarat, numbers fewer than 150, and is protected through the modified power-line directions.
accepted.tq: Check the species range, numerical estimate and modified legal measure separately.
accepted.sec: Bird sanctuaries and species projects → state (first bird sanctuary, Project Tiger, Project Cheetah, GIB case)

accepted.s: The Great Indian Bustard power-line case before the Supreme Court is identified as:
o: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
Wildlife First v. State of Rajasthan
T.N. Godavarman v. Union of India
M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India
accepted.x: The case is M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India. It concerned measures to reduce power-line threats to the Great Indian Bustard.
accepted.tq: Use the exact litigant name and case title as the discriminating fact.
accepted.sec: Bird sanctuaries and species projects → state (first bird sanctuary, Project Tiger, Project Cheetah, GIB case)

accepted.s: The first artificial-insemination breeding of the Great Indian Bustard was conducted at:
accepted.x: The first artificial-insemination breeding of the Great Indian Bustard was conducted at Jaisalmer.
accepted.tq: Test the specific location associated with the conservation intervention.
accepted.sec: Bird sanctuaries and species projects → state (first bird sanctuary, Project Tiger, Project Cheetah, GIB case)

accepted.s: The National Forest Policy, 1988 envisages forest and tree cover over what percentage of India’s total area?
accepted.x: The National Forest Policy, 1988 set a target of 33% of the total area under forest and tree cover.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the national target from the separate hill-and-mountain target.
accepted.sec: Forest policy and law - National Forest Policy 1988 targets, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980

accepted.s: Under the National Forest Policy, 1988, the target for forest and tree cover in hills and mountains is:
accepted.x: The National Forest Policy, 1988 prescribed a target of 66% forest and tree cover in hills and mountains.
accepted.tq: Compare the general 33% target with the higher physiographic-region target.
accepted.sec: Forest policy and law - National Forest Policy 1988 targets, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980

accepted.s: India’s forest and tree cover, as stated in the current assessment, is approximately:
accepted.x: India’s forest and tree cover is stated as 25.17%, compared with the National Forest Policy target of 33%.
accepted.tq: Separate the present percentage from the policy target and historical figures.
accepted.sec: Forest policy and law - National Forest Policy 1988 targets, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980

accepted.s: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires which of the following before forest land is diverted for non-forest purposes?
o: Approval only of the district collector
Approval only of the State Legislature
Approval of the National Tiger Conservation Authority
accepted.x: Diversion of forest land under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires central approval.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority exercises the decisive approval power.
accepted.sec: Forest policy and law - National Forest Policy 1988 targets, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980

accepted.s: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 was renamed as:
accepted.x: The Act was renamed the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980.
accepted.tq: Choose the exact official expression rather than a semantically similar title.
accepted.sec: Forest policy and law - National Forest Policy 1988 targets, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980

accepted.s: Which institution manages the compensatory afforestation funds generated under the forest conservation framework?
accepted.x: CAMPA manages the compensatory afforestation funds.
accepted.tq: Match the environmental institution with its specific financial function.
accepted.sec: Forest policy and law - National Forest Policy 1988 targets, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh diverted how much forest land under the Forest (Conservation) Act during April–December 2025?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh diverted 149.57 hectares under the Forest (Conservation) Act during April–December 2025.
accepted.tq: Read the decimal figure precisely and avoid transposition of digits.
